## Upcoming patches[]

As of 2026, *Fallout 76* for the most part follows a standard schedule of a major update release and a subsequent supporting patch, with approximately four of these major release cycles per year (in spring, summer, autumn and winter). This accounts for eight patches per year: four titled releases, and four bug-fix patches supporting each of the titled releases. Game director Jonathan Rush stated in March 2026 that summer and winter releases are meant for large new content drops, while those in spring and fall are intended for improving pre-existing content. [1] 

Among the upcoming releases for *Fallout 76* is a "part two" to the story of the *Burning Springs* update, as Bethesda Game Studios have confirmed *Burning Springs* is only the first entry in a story spanning multiple chapters and updates. [2] Certain areas of the Burning Springs region are inaccessible behind invisible barriers, potentially for future content, as the development team has stated they would prefer to reserve areas for the future, rather than bulldoze player C.A.M.P.s when new content is added to existing areas. [3] 

During the Fallout Day Broadcast on October 23, 2025, Rush and Bill LaCoste announced that an update in 2026 would feature hardware improvements for *Fallout 76* on PS5 and Xbox Series X. [4] 

In March 2026, Rush alluded to patch 76 being a major update for *Fallout 76*, claiming that "heads are going to explode" when it is able to be revealed; [1] prior to this, patch 76 being a milestone update was first teased in October 2025. [5] Under the game's current schedule, patch 76 would tentatively fall within summer 2027.

In April 2026, Rush said *Fallout 76* has "plans for years down the road" and the development team has "more ideas than what we know what to do with." [6]
